sustainable farming = growing food in a way that can continue without ruining soil, water or wildlife
sustainable seafood = fish caught or farmed in a way that does not empty the oceans
seasonal produce = fruit and vegetables harvested at the natural time of year
locally sourced = obtained from nearby farms or producers
food labelling = the information printed on packaging about ingredients and nutrition
traceability = the ability to follow a food back to where it was produced
supply chain = the sequence of steps that takes food from farm to shop
supermarket chain = a company that owns many large food shops
food shortage = a situation in which there is not enough food available
food desert = a neighbourhood with few shops selling fresh, healthy food
food bank = a charity that gives donated food to people who cannot afford it
food poverty = not being able to afford enough healthy food
ultra-processed = made mostly from industrial ingredients rather than whole foods
convenience food = food that is quick to prepare, often packaged or ready-made
ready meal = a complete dish sold cooked, which you only need to heat
trans fat = an industrial fat, now widely restricted, that harms heart health
cholesterol = a fatty substance in blood; some foods can affect its level
sugar tax = a government charge on drinks with a lot of added sugar
compostable packaging = wrapping that can break down into soil in a compost bin
artificial sweetener = a chemical used instead of sugar to make food taste sweet
